criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixture records for a landed job with a CI wait and a rebuild. Running `cargo test -p athena-core status` shows the landing stage reports their duration (it covers the wait and the rebuild, not just verifier end to outcome).
criteria.evidence: The test the_landing_stage_covers_the_wait_and_rebuild_recorded_after_the_outcome passes, but its only fixture for the 'CI wait and rebuild' is a 405 Merge HostError (landing_refusal). No fixture models a CI wait or a rebuild. HostErrorLog::record (gh/transport.rs:314-334) writes a host error only for a refused call. So for a normal landing with no refusal, landing_end falls back to the outcome, which run/mod.rs:1850-1856 sets right after verification. The stage stays verifier end to outcome (the reported 0.1 min). The `landings/` record (athena-data history.rs:221, with created_at and commits[].job, written after the merge per gh/records.rs:23-25) is not read.

criteria.criterion: A new test dispatches a job, runs it 20 minutes, and closes it days later. `cargo test -p athena-core status` shows it contributes 20 minutes to the 'did not land' figure, not the multi-day span.
criteria.evidence: The test a_job_run_for_twenty_minutes_and_closed_days_later_spent_twenty_minutes passes. It asserts unlanded_minutes == 20.0 for an abandoned job whose 20-minute producer run is followed by an outcome 3 days later.

criteria.criterion: A test shows idle time between jobs is computed from time spent, so a job left open for days does not hide the gap. Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`.
criteria.evidence: The same test asserts idle_minutes == 50 + 4360. The gap after the abandoned job's last invocation counts in full, not the 40 minutes it would be if measured from the closing record. busy_intervals replaces working_span in Throughput::compute.

criteria.criterion: A test on `Throughput::text` output shows each figure in the section (landed per day, median per landed job and its stages, idle between jobs, did not land) states its basis, naming the records it was measured from. `athena status` prints that text, so the basis shows there.
criteria.evidence: every_throughput_figure_prints_the_records_it_was_measured_from passes. It checks that the line after each of the four figures holds 'basis:' and names the records. The landing part of the stage basis is misleading, though: it says the CI wait and rebuild have no record of their own, but the landings/ record exists (see findings).

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the corrected landing, unlanded and idle figures and the printed bases.
criteria.evidence: A Fixed entry in CHANGELOG.md covers landing and rebuild, did not land, idle, and the basis lines. Its landing claim ('they have no record of their own'; 'the landing records are not part of the job records') is inaccurate about the landings/ record.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed (1668 tests).

criteria.criterion: No path other than crates/athena-core/src/status.rs and CHANGELOG.md changes. No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) changes.
criteria.evidence: Changed: CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. hestia.rs is on the expected deliverables list, which is the scope statement, and its change only updates the throughput review prompt text. No governance file changed.

findings.summary: The landing-and-rebuild figure is still wrong for every ordinary landing: it is extended only by host refusal records, not by the landing record the user named.
findings.evidence: landing_end takes the later of the closing outcome and the newest WorkPhase::Landing host error. Host errors are written only for refused calls (gh/transport.rs:314-334). The Landed outcome is set right after verification (run/mod.rs:1850-1856), before the CI wait and push. A successful landing with no refusals therefore still measures verifier end to outcome, about 0.1 min, the bug reported. The landings/ record (athena-data history.rs:221: created_at, commits[].job; written after the merge per gh/records.rs:23-25) marks the end of the CI wait and push and is never read. The accepted reading said to add the smallest reader in status.rs if it is not reachable from JobRecords. Fix: read the landing records, match them to jobs by commits[].job, and use max(outcome, landing.created_at) as the landing end, with a test built from such a record.

findings.summary: The criterion-1 test stands in a 405 host refusal for the CI wait and rebuild, so it passes without testing the requested behavior.
findings.evidence: The only post-outcome fixture is landing_refusal(job, 10:17), a HostError with status 405 and operation Merge. A real CI wait plus rebuild leaves no such record, so the test does not show the stage covering them.

findings.summary: The printed basis and the CHANGELOG tell readers the CI wait and rebuild have no record, while a landing record exists.
findings.evidence: The basis says 'because the CI wait and the rebuild have no record of their own'. The CHANGELOG says 'the landing records are not part of the job records'. The throughput review reads this text and ranks proposals by these figures, so it inherits the wrong landing figure and the misleading explanation.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/status.rs Throughput::text; CHANGELOG.md; crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs throughput prompt

findings.summary: Time spent leaves out the 'waits recorded for the job' that the request lists.
findings.evidence: time_spent sums invocation wall times and check_minutes only. The request defines time spent as 'the sum of invocation wall times, check durations and waits recorded for the job'.

findings.summary: Check time in the idle calculation is placed by estimate, not measured.
findings.evidence: The checks interval is set to end where the first verifier started, or to begin at the last invocation's end when there is no verifier. That is an estimate of when the checks ran, not a recorded interval. It is acceptable, but the basis line does not say it is an estimate.

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The request says to measure landing "from the verifier's end to the landing record and the rebuild's end". The accepted reading says that if landing records can't be reached from JobRecords, the producer should add a small reader in status.rs. The candidate instead says landing records are not part of the job records. It stands in the newest landing-phase host refusal, a record written only when the host refuses a call. So the landing figure stays the same for an ordinary successful landing. Time spent also leaves out the "waits recorded for the job" that the request lists.

The accepted reading says that if landing records can't be reached from JobRecords, the producer should add a small reader in status.rs. The candidate instead says landing records are not part of the job records. It stands in the newest landing-phase host refusal, a record written only when the host refuses a call. So the landing figure stays the same for an ordinary successful landing. Time spent also leaves out the "waits recorded for the job" that the request lists.
summary: The did-not-land and idle figures are fixed: both now use time spent (invocation wall times plus check durations, and busy intervals), and new tests show a job that ran 20 minutes and closed days later counts 20 minutes and no longer hides the idle gap. Every throughput figure now prints a basis line, and fmt, clippy and the tests pass on Athena's records. The landing-and-rebuild figure is not fixed. The landed outcome is written just after the verifier, before the CI wait, push and rebuild. The candidate extends the stage only to the newest landing-phase host refusal, which exists only when the host refused a call. An ordinary landing therefore still reports about 0.1 minute. The `landings/` record the user named is ignored, although it is written after the merge and carries a `created_at` time and each commit's job. The criterion-1 test passes only because it uses a 405 refusal record as a stand-in for the CI wait and rebuild. The printed basis and the CHANGELOG also wrongly say the wait and rebuild have no record. Verdict: fail.
